result.title: How Much Gradient Does Truncated Backprop Lose in Looped Transformers?
result.comment: 31 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables. Code, pre-registrations and results: https://github.com/Aur-Shalev-Merin/lost-gradient-looped-transformers
result.summary: Looped transformers reuse one block of layers many times and are often trained by backpropagating through only the last k loops. We measure how much of the weight gradient this throws away, exactly and for every k from one backward pass, on nine looped language models, and report three findings. First, on a trained model this lost gradient is set near the output: once the loop count is well above k, it barely changes with the loop count (within about 0.03 from 32 to 64 loops on the three models we tested, as a pre-registered test predicted for Parcae). Where the backward signal shrinks, $ρ^k$, with $ρ$ the signal's fitted shrink per loop, approximates it at moderate loop counts but overstates it at long ones, because the fitted $ρ$ drifts up as the fit takes in more loops. On Ouro the signal grows, and keeping two of four loops still loses 81% of the final output's gradient. Second, the lost gradient falls during fine-tuning, by 0.07-0.22 within 300 steps on three of four models, on held-out problems too. The fall is not just the read-out's share of the gradient; training only the layers outside the loop reproduced up to half of it, and it also falls under truncated training. So a trained model's value overstates what truncation removes later. Third, we could not show that it predicts the training cost of truncation better than rules that need no measurement: on two new models it tied Parcae's cost at the same k, in a test too small to separate them.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在九个循环语言模型上精确测量了只对最后 k 次循环反传所丢弃的权重梯度，并考察它随循环长度与微调的变化，以及能否预测截断训练的实际代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 循环块复用与截断反传直接对应循环式 latent 推理的训练监督和贡献分配问题；其「丢失梯度集中于输出附近、随循环数变化不大」的观察，可供核查深层循环状态是否实际获得监督。
